Reshaped this. I originally submitted a client-side one-liner in `dialog-session-list.tsx`,
which was the wrong shape, and I said so on #51144 — the short version is that `dev` already
fixes this properly and I had misread which code path the dev TUI calls.

What changed:

- Dropped the TUI change. `dev`'s `sessionListQuery()` still sends `""` and relies on the
  server guard, so client-side handling diverges from the reference implementation.
- Moved the fix into `packages/core/src/session/store.ts:112` and ported **only** `dev`'s
  truthiness guard. I did *not* port its nested-subdirectory or `NULL`-path branches — I had
  originally done so, then measured why that was wrong and narrowed it. My later comment on this
  PR has the reasoning and the numbers.
- Rebased onto the current `v2` tip.
- Tests moved from the TUI query assertions to `packages/core/test/session-store.test.ts`, where
  they assert the actual returned rows. The two tests each pin one decision: the empty-subpath
  test fails if the `NULL` branch is added, the exact-match test fails if a subtree branch is
  added (I checked each widening separately).
- Documented `subpath` on the query schemas, since this changes what an empty value means.

Net: 4 files, one commit. Same issue, same root cause, but now it's the backport it
should have been. Still happy to reshape if you'd prefer it client-side or split differently.

I looked into this on the current `dev` head and the mechanism is now pinned. Your A/B isolation is what makes it visible.

**Where the two paths diverge.** The autocomplete builds its slash list from two sources (`packages/tui/src/component/prompt/autocomplete.tsx`):

- built-in commands come from `useCommandSlashes()` (`packages/tui/src/keymap.tsx:286`), whose `onSelect` is `keymap.dispatchCommand(entry.command.name)` — it **executes** the command;
- file-defined commands come from `sync.data.command` (`autocomplete.tsx:450-463`), whose `onSelect` only **rewrites the input text** to `"/" + name + " "` and moves the cursor. It never executes and never submits.

`select()` (`autocomplete.tsx:553-558`) is what runs on Enter (bound at `:611-618` as `prompt.autocomplete.select`): it calls `hide()` and then `onSelect?.()`. For a built-in that dispatches the command. For a file command it just re-inserts `/name ` — exactly the "cursor advances one space, nothing is submitted" step you observed. The second Enter then submits the completed line through the normal prompt path.

**One correction to the body:** the template body appearing in the chat as literal user input is expected — for file commands the template IS the prompt that gets sent, so that symptom is the normal path, not a second defect. The real defect is narrower than the original report: the first Enter is consumed by the completion even when the typed text already names the command exactly, so file commands need two Enters while built-ins need one.

**Fix direction** (small, one file): when the selected file command already matches the typed text exactly, Enter should submit instead of re-completing. `Autocomplete` currently has no submit callback among its props (`autocomplete.tsx:75-86`), so this is either a `submit` prop threaded in from the prompt, or the autocomplete declining to consume Enter on an exact match.

I would like to work on this. Plan: base on `dev`, keep the change to the file-command branch of the completion path, and cover both cases (exact match submits, partial match still completes) with a test in the prompt autocomplete suite.

Releasing my claim here so my in-flight work stays bounded — I am picking up a smaller target on the default branch instead. Nothing is withdrawn as analysis: the measured numbers and the corrected fix site in my earlier comments still stand (`packages/session-ui/src/components/message-part.css:1472-1477`, with the `:1479-1497` local-session halves as the precedent in the same file). Anyone is welcome to take it, and I am happy to hand over the details.

@olliecurtis Since your report lists OpenCode 1.18.31, here's how to install V2 on macOS:

1. If V1 was installed with a package manager, remove that V1 installation with the same package manager first so an older `opencode` binary isn't still first on your PATH. Keep your configuration and session data; `opencode uninstall` can remove shared data unless you explicitly use its keep flags.
2. Install V2 using **one** of these methods:
   - Homebrew: `brew install anomalyco/tap/opencode-v2`
   - Shell installer: `curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/v2/install | bash` (replaces the V1 curl-installed binary)
   - npm: `npm install -g @opencode/cli`
3. Run `opencode --version` to confirm it shows `2.x`, then start `opencode` in your project and check your provider/model setup.

Your supported V1 configuration can be read by V2 without an immediate rewrite, but V1 plugins and integrations using the server API need migration. See the [V2 installation guide](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/) and [V1 → V2 migration guide](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/migrate-v1). If the same Azure Responses failure occurs on V2, please file a new issue with your V2 version and a redacted request/response; we haven't verified your particular Azure gateway.

Two notes on choices I made that aren't visible in the diff.

**`packages/protocol/openapi.json` is not regenerated.** This adds a description to the `subpath`
query params, but the committed document is already stale on `v2` independent of this change — on a
pristine `v2` tree, `bun run --cwd packages/protocol check:generated` fails with *"Generated OpenAPI
document is stale"*, and regenerating produces 126 lines, of which this change is
exactly 1 — the `subpath` description. The other 125 pick up endpoints like `/api/pair` that were
added to the code without a regeneration. Folding that into a one-line bug
fix looked worse than leaving the generated file alone, so I did. Happy to send the regeneration as a
separate PR if that's the preferred shape.

**This is deliberately narrower than `dev`.** `dev` fixes the same bug at
`packages/opencode/src/session/session.ts:967-977`, but it also matches nested subdirectories and `NULL`
paths. I left both out:

- `NULL` does not mean "at the project root". `session.path` arrived via
  `20260428004200_add_session_path.ts`, a bare `ALTER TABLE session ADD path text` with no backfill
  of `NULL` anywhere in `packages/core/src/database/` (the only later `UPDATE session SET path`,
  `20260601010001_normalize_storage_paths.ts:18`, is guarded by `path IS NOT NULL` and only
  normalises backslashes), and the v1→v2 copy selects `path` verbatim
  (`v1-migration.bun.ts:612`, `:618`, `:790`). So `NULL` means "this column was never populated", not "at the project root". On
  the install I measured, 2 of the 34 top-level `NULL` rows are below their project root, so folding
  them into every subtree query would surface them wrongly. `dev` gets away with it because it
  constrains that branch with `eq(directory, …)`; a project-scoped `v2` query has no such conjunct.
- Nested matching changes a filter that currently works, and nothing in this bug needs it.

Each test pins one decision: the empty-subpath test fails if the `NULL` branch is added, the
exact-match test fails if a nested-subtree branch is added. I checked each widening on its own
rather than only in combination.

One more thing worth knowing: `subpath` only reaches the filter for non-global projects — the TUI sends
`directory` instead for the global one (`dialog-session-list.tsx:66-70`). That condition is what makes
dropping the subpath filter safe, since project scoping is a separate conjunct in the store.

`dev` is the 1.18.x line and this is the 2.0.x line, so the two are separate rather than one being
stale. Happy to reshape toward the full `dev` semantics, or the client-side variant, if you'd prefer.

Please remove it or replace it with a brief summary in your own words focused on what you observed. The needs:compliance label will remain until that is addressed.

## Additional Context

### Reproduction Scenario

The crash occurred while running **8 parallel agents in separate processes** simultaneously. Each agent was working on different tasks across multiple workspaces.

### Debug Bundle

Full debug bundle exported at `2026-09-26T18:00:23Z` is available upon request. It contains:

- `crashpad/` — crash dumps
- `server-1/opencode.log` — server logs
- `desktop/20260926T173503/` — desktop logs (crash.log, main.log, renderer.log, server.log, pty.log, window.log, network.log)
- `manifest.json` — app metadata

### Key Log Evidence

**window.log** — OOM crash:
```
[2026-09-26 21:00:17.733] [error] (window) app render process gone {
  url: 'oc://renderer/index.html',
  details: { reason: 'oom', exitCode: -536870904 }
}
```

**renderer.log** — ResizeObserver loop storm:
- 15866+ `ResizeObserver loop completed with undelivered notifications` errors across 5 sessions
- `Failed to update terminal Error: PTY session not found: pty_0de7a0dc9001cRgCl9QF2xOtjF`
- `[ghostty-vt] warning(stream): unimplemented mode: 9001`

**pty.log** — PTY session leak:
```
[2026-09-26 20:35:11.886] [info] (pty) console {
  level: 3,
  message: 'Failed to update terminal Error: PTY session not found: pty_0de7a0dc9001cRgCl9QF2xOtjF',
}
```

### System Details

- **OS:** Windows 11 (win32 x64)
- **OpenCode:** 1.18.32
- **Electron:** 42.3.3
- **Chrome:** 148.0.7778.218
- **Node:** 24.15.0
- **Uptime before crash:** ~1520 seconds (~25 minutes)
- **Workspaces open:** 7+ projects (MSCodeBase, Stanford-Town-AI-Project, devbase, etc.)

### Related Issues

- #36218: Windows Desktop renderer OOM crash (same exit code)
- #38296: ResizeObserver loop storm (same error pattern)
- #33712: Desktop renderer crash with ResizeObserver feedback loop

### Source Code Analysis

I analyzed the opencode source code (cloned from `anomalyco/opencode`). The issue appears to be caused by a combination of:

1. **ResizeObserver loop** in `packages/app/src/pages/session.tsx` — multiple `createResizeObserver` calls that trigger `fill()` → `loadOlder()` → content resize → ResizeObserver again
2. **PTY session leak** — terminal sessions not properly cleaned up
3. **ghostty-web terminal** — large scrollback buffer (10,000 lines)
4. **Multiple workspaces** — 7+ projects loaded simultaneously

The crash is more likely with parallel agents because each agent generates continuous output, triggering more ResizeObserver callbacks and PTY updates.

I need to correct two things I said on #51144, because this PR does the opposite of both and the
thread reads as if it doesn't.

**I was wrong that the server guard should stay `!== undefined`.** My original claim was factually
right — `Session.create` does store `''` for a session started at the project root
(`packages/core/src/session.ts:270`), and relaxing the guard *does* mean `subpath=''` can no longer
select root-level sessions only. `store.ts:112` is the only path conjunct in that query, so that set
is no longer expressible server-side. What was wrong was my judgment that this capability was worth
preserving. I could not find a caller that needs it: the only caller of this filter in the whole `v2`
tree is `dialog-session-list.tsx:70`, and it wants the *whole* project when you sit at the root. A
client that genuinely wants root-only can still fetch the project list and post-filter. `dev` makes
the same trade, and its TUI relies on the server guard doing so.

**I was also wrong to carry over `dev`'s `NULL` branch.** I said in that thread that `or`, `isNull` and
`like` were all available so the branches could be ported across. They port fine mechanically; the
problem is what the `NULL` branch *means*. `dev` constrains it with `eq(directory, …)`
(`session.ts:976`) because `dev` has a `directory` conjunct to constrain it with. A project-scoped
`v2` query has none, so the branch is unconstrained there — and `NULL` does not mean "at the project
root". The column was added by a bare `ALTER TABLE session ADD path text`
(`20260428004200_add_session_path.ts`) with no backfill of `NULL` anywhere in
`packages/core/src/database/` — the only later `UPDATE session SET path`
(`20260601010001_normalize_storage_paths.ts:18`) is guarded by `path IS NOT NULL` and just normalises
backslashes. The v1 source column is nullable and is copied verbatim
(`v1-migration.bun.ts:612`, `:618`, `:790`). So `NULL` means "never populated", and on the install I
measured, 2 of the 34 top-level `NULL` rows are below their project root — folding them into every
subtree query would surface them wrongly. So this ports `dev`'s truthiness guard and leaves the two
branches that need a `directory` conjunct behind.

**On the two tests, precisely:** each pins one decision, not both. The empty-subpath test fails if the
`NULL` branch is added; the exact-match test fails if a nested-subtree branch is added. I checked each
widening on its own rather than only as a combination.

**One more change to the diff since my last comment:** I tightened two claims after review. `info.ts:51`
maps `''` and `NULL` to no subpath, so the filter now agrees with *it* — `projector.ts:292` still maps
only `NULL` and deliberately keeps `''`, and I left that alone. And the `subpath` description now says
an empty value "applies no path filter" rather than "returns every session in the project", which would
have been wrong when `project` is omitted.

If you'd rather keep root-only filtering expressible, the fix is a separate explicit parameter rather
than overloading `''` — say the word and I'll do that instead.

Correction to my own earlier comments on this issue, now that the PR (#51514) is up — it does the
opposite of what I recommended here, so the thread shouldn't be read without this.

- I said the server guard should stay `!== undefined` to keep root-only filtering. My reasoning was
  right about the mechanism but I had the priority backwards: I could not find any caller of that
  filter in the `v2` tree that needs root-only — the only one is the session picker, which wants the
  whole project at a project root. So the guard is relaxed. The trade is real and I should have said
  it earlier: `subpath=''` no longer selects root-level sessions only.
- I said `dev`'s nested and `NULL` branches could be carried across behind the same truthiness guard.
  They port mechanically, but the `NULL` branch is the problem: `dev` constrains it with
  `eq(directory, …)` and a project-scoped `v2` query has no such conjunct, while `NULL` means "this
  column was never populated" (bare `ALTER TABLE` with no backfill) rather than "at the project root"
  — 2 of the 34 top-level `NULL` rows on my install are below their root. So the PR ports only the
  truthiness guard.

The measurement tables in my first comment still stand.

**What needs to be fixed:**

**Confirming on `opencode 1.3.3` (Sep 26, 2026) — controlled repro, production gap math, and a headless-visibility angle that hasn't been covered above.**

**Controlled repro** — local mock provider returning `500` with only `content-type` in the response headers (no `retry-after`), body `mock upstream error`:

Observed inter-attempt deltas: `2.03s / 4.01s / 8.01s / 16.02s / 32.02s / 64.02s` — a perfect x2 ladder from `RETRY_INITIAL_DELAY * 2^(attempt-1)` with no cap applied, and the process emits **zero output** for the entire ladder.

**Production gap quantization** (fingerprint for anyone triaging mystery "hangs"): multi-hour silent stalls observed in production run logs land on exact ladder sums. During one provider outage window we recorded silent gaps of ~4.55h / 9.1h / 18.2h / 36.4h; e.g. the 36.4h case is 131,084.8s vs the ladder sum `Σ(2s .. 2^16s) = 131,070s` plus ~1s/attempt overhead across 15 attempts. If an automated run looks "hung" and the silence is a power-of-two multiple of ~2 seconds, it is this ladder, not a deadlock — worth checking before assuming a transport/CLI bug.

**Headless impact (distinct from the UI-stuck reports above):** `opencode run --format json` emits *nothing* during retries — `SessionStatus.set({type:"retry"})` is internal-only and no retry-status part is emitted on the run stream. For programmatic consumers (CI, agent harnesses), a run inside the ladder is indistinguishable from a dead process. Also note the SDK layer is called with `retries ?? 0`, so all retrying funnels into this session loop — there is no second safety net. A retry-status event on the run stream would make this whole failure class observable.

**Fix scope:** #33733 is the right first step — the 30s `RETRY_MAX_DELAY_NO_HEADERS` cap is effectively dead in production because real 5xx responses almost always carry headers. But even with the delay capped, the processor loop keeps its unbounded attempt count, so a persistent outage retries forever at the cap and the run never surfaces a terminal error. End-to-end close = delay cap (#33733) + max-attempts bound + a retry event on the run stream.

Confirming this failure mode is still reproducible in production as of Sep 26, 2026 (opencode 1.3.3, controlled repro + production gap math posted on #17648). The delay cap in this PR is the highest-value first step — the no-headers cap is effectively dead for real 5xx responses since they always carry headers. One gap left even with this merged: the processor retry loop still has no attempt bound, so a persistent outage retries forever at the cap and never surfaces a terminal error.

**Description:**
When resolving the custom provider model `atria/atria-dawn-preview`, `ModelResolver.resolveCatalogModel` throws an exception and the entire session fails to load. This error appears in the UI as **"unavailable on this server"** and prevents any new provider from being added.
